Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
6:01 AM

People in India are switching to UPI because paying now feels as easy as sending a message. You use one phone and one app, and money moves between bank accounts in seconds, at any hour, including holidays.

Three reasons stand out:

It's free and instant. Most payments between people and to shops cost nothing, and the money arrives straight away.
It works everywhere. A single QR code is enough, from a chai stall to a large mall. Shopkeepers don't need a card machine, and you don't need to carry cash or hunt for change.
It's simple and safe. You pay with a phone number or QR code and confirm with your PIN, so you never hand over your card or account details.

Timing helped too. Cheap smartphones and low-cost mobile data spread across the country just as UPI launched in 2016. The 2016 cash shortage pushed many first-time users to try it. Because UPI is an open system run by NPCI, any bank or app can plug into it, so people can pick the app they like and still pay anyone.

The result is that small vendors, students and families in villages and big cities all use the same everyday habit. Once people try it, going back to cash feels slow.
